content.text: {"title":"The Cinnamon Button Exchange","premise":"At a tiny bakery stall, Ada has baked one cinnamon button for a neighborhood tasting. Pip the squirrel proudly labels every bun himself, while Nia arrives hungry with a jar of bright red berry jam. A swapped label, a proud refusal, or an unexpected taste can turn the same little snack into three very different celebrations.","cast_and_props":"Characters: ada (child baker; wants Nia to enjoy her baking), pip (proud squirrel; wants his labels admired), nia (neighbor; wants a fair, filling exchange). Props: stall, button (cinnamon pastry), berryjar (Nia's jam), label (a paper label), basket (Ada's pastry basket). State slots include button.owner, button.mark, button.location, berryjar.owner, berryjar.open, label.text, label.attached, ada.knows.label.text, pip.knows.button.mark, nia.knows.button.mark, ada.agreement, pip.agreement, nia.content, and button.shared.","kernels_and_interactions":"1. Observation/telling: Pip observes the button's actual mark; Ada can tell Nia or Pip what she baked. Knowledge enables choosing whether to exchange, relabel, or taste. 2. Ownership transfer: Nia may transfer berryjar to Ada; Ada may transfer button to Nia, but only while the relevant owner is correct. 3. Labeling: Pip attaches label.text='pepper' or 'cinnamon' to the button, creating mistaken belief without changing the pastry. Ada can remove or correct the label after learning its text. 4. Tasting/exchange: Nia tastes the button only if she knows or accepts its label; the result sets nia.content and button.shared. 5. Agreement: characters can accept a fair exchange, a shared tasting, or Pip's corrected label. These kernels interact through ownership, knowledge, and the physical label rather than abstract counters.","seed_parameters":"build(seed) uses random.Random(seed). Seed-derived initial conditions: button.mark is cinnamon for most seeds, but may be 'pepper' for a deliberately savory batch; label.text is either 'cinnamon' or 'pepper'; label.attached is true; berryjar.open is false; button.owner is 'ada'; berryjar.owner is 'nia'. Seeds also choose whether Nia begins believing the label, whether Pip knows the true mark, and whether Ada has promised a taste or a trade. premise_keys: button.mark, label.text, nia.belief, berryjar.owner. outcome_keys: button.owner, nia.content, pip.agreement, button.shared.","candidate_scenes":"Use 15–18 candidates, 5–10 selected. Opening candidates establish Ada's invitation and the label's visible claim. Shared scenes: inspect_label (Ada observes label.text), ask_pip (Ada asks Pip what he meant), tell_mark (Ada tells Nia button.mark), offer_jar (Nia offers berryjar), correct_label (Pip or Ada changes label.text), trade_button (Ada transfers button to Nia), open_jar (Nia opens berryjar), taste_button (Nia tastes button), share_button (Nia and Ada agree to share), and final_bow (Pip agrees the label is right). Branch-specific scenes: Nia refuses a pepper-labeled sweet and requests jam; Pip insists his cinnamon label is right; or the savory seed makes the label accidentally correct and the group invents a daring sweet-and-savory tasting. Reuse inspect_label, tell_mark, offer_jar, open_jar, and trade_button across paths. Mark only taste_button and one pivotal agreement scene as pivotal.","constraints":"Every slot is declared before use and all state keys begin with an existing entity ID. No character may speak as knowing button.mark before observing or being told it. transfer requires current ownership. taste_button requires button.owner='nia', berryjar.open=true, and either nia knows the mark or nia.agreement='brave_taste'. The inciting action is Pip attaching the label before Ada responds. Goal accepts nia.content=true, with distinct outcomes: nia.content='sweet_trade', 'savory_surprise', or 'shared_treat'. Use prune=True, 3–5 kernel families, 12–22 candidates, and no counters.","different_endings":"1. Sweet trade: Nia owns and enjoys the cinnamon button after giving Ada the opened berry jar; final image: Pip wears the corrected label like a tiny sash. 2. Savory surprise: the pepper-marked button is tasted with berry jam, and Nia declares it astonishing; final image: three jammy pawprints circle the empty plate. 3. Shared treat: Ada keeps ownership but breaks the button into pieces for everyone; final image: the label hangs from the stall while crumbs form a little cinnamon constellation. Each ending needs two guarded prose variants and must describe only actions actually selected."}
